map.算法：温度按 Arrhenius Q10=2，超过材料上限取 0.05，否则 =: Algorithm: temperature by Arrhenius Q10 = 2, above material upper limit takes 0.05, otherwise 2 to the power of ((suitable temperature minus operating temperature) / 10), lower bound 0.01; pressure factor = e to the power of (minus p / 20); speed factor = e to the power of (minus speed / 5000) (static takes 1); media factor: oil 1, water 0.9, gas 0.7, chemical 0.6; estimated life = base life times four factors (lower bound 10 h). PV: linear velocity = speed times 0.05 times pi / 60, PV = pressure times linear velocity, limit PTFE 0.5, others 0.3 MPa m/s. Base life: NBR 8000 h, FKM 15000 h, EPDM 12000 h, VMQ 10000 h, PTFE 25000 h.
map.例：丁腈橡胶 NBR（基准 8000h、适宜 80℃、上限 120℃）、油介质、: Example: nitrile rubber NBR (base 8000 h, suitable 80 C, upper limit 120 C), oil media, 80 C / 5 MPa / 1500 rpm gives temperature factor 1, pressure factor 0.779, speed factor 0.741, estimated life 4616 h (about 192 days), linear velocity 3.93 m/s, PV = 19.64 MPa m/s exceeds limit, grade medium. Temperature rises to 130 C (exceeds NBR limit) gives temperature factor drops sharply to 0.05, life only 231 h, prompts temperature exceeds material limit, need to change material. Switch to PTFE (base 25000 h, suitable 150 C) at 150 C / 2 MPa / 500 rpm gives three factors 1 / 0.905 / 0.905, life 20468 h (about 853 days), grade excellent.
map.PV 值为什么会超限？: Why does the PV value exceed the limit?
The PV limit is a conservative reference under dry friction / boundary lubrication. This example 5 MPa times 3.93 m/s = 19.6 far exceeds 0.3, indicating this condition must ensure adequate lubrication and heat dissipation, or switch to a low-friction material and reduce linear velocity; if there is a good oil film in practice, relax per the manufacturer PV curve.
map.温度为什么影响这么大？: Why does temperature matter so much?
map.Q10=2 表示温度每升高 10℃ 老化速率翻倍、寿命减半；一旦超过材料上限，因: Q10 = 2 means every 10 C rise doubles the aging rate and halves life; once the material upper limit is exceeded, the factor directly takes 0.05 (only 5% life left). Therefore the upper limit temperature is a hard constraint in material selection, followed by optimizing pressure and speed.
